task:
Shotcut is already open with /home/user/Documents/filter_project.mlt (1920x1080, 30 fps). The project already contains one clip on the V1 timeline track referencing /home/user/Videos/source.mp4.

Steps:
1. Click the clip on the V1 timeline so it is selected.
2. Open the Filters panel (top toolbar or via the Filters menu).
3. Click the '+' button in the Filters panel to add a new filter.
4. Choose the VIDEO category and pick the 'Brightness' filter.
5. Leave the default brightness value; press Ctrl+S to save.

After saving, the project must still contain the existing clip and have a Brightness video filter applied to it.

verification.description: The source.mp4 clip is still in the project
A Brightness filter is present in the project

cli_feasibility.translation: Use CLI: project open filter_project.mlt, filter add brightness --track 1 --clip 0, project save
cli_feasibility.reason: ✅ CLI-Anything shotcut supports filter add with --track and --clip parameters. The CLI can add filters to specific clips on tracks. Task mentions GUI steps (click, Filters panel) but CLI can accomplish the same outcome.
